risks.description: Overall envelope 671.1 x 443.9 x approximately 309 mm exceeds the published vmc_3axis X/Y travels, so machining must use dedicated SPM fixtures, indexed setups, or qualified large-capacity partner support.
risks.mitigation: Use spm_milling_drilling with tool-room designed modular fixtures; verify actual machine envelope before order release.

risks.description: Several H7 holes, central bores, counterbores, pockets and section cavities have missing or partly legible depths/diameters.
risks.mitigation: Release route as provisional; obtain native CAD/released drawing values before CNC programming and fixture/gauge design.

risks.description: Large asymmetric 15CDV6 housing heat treated to 31-38 HRC can distort; H7 holes and precision bores must retain position after post-HT finishing.
risks.mitigation: Rough/semi-machine before HT, leave finishing stock on precision bores and datum surfaces, use controlled quench, and perform post-HT grinding/honing/verification.

risks.description: Shop profile lists in-house alkaline zinc plating; cadmium plating chemistry is specified but not explicitly confirmed.
risks.mitigation: Confirm whether plating_line is approved for cadmium 8-12 microns; otherwise qualify an outside cadmium plating supplier and hydrogen-embrittlement bake.

outside_processes_needed.reason: Large complex high-strength 15CDV6 housing would waste excessive material from block; forging/premachined near-net blank is required or strongly preferred for quantity 150.
Final part specification requires 31-38 HRC; heat treatment is listed as outside vendor capability in the shop profile.
outside_processes_needed.sequence_position: after soft machining and pre-HT deburr

outside_processes_needed.reason: Post-HT datum recovery and H7/H8 precision bores require grinding/honing; these are outside processes in the shop profile.
Large housing has position tolerances down to 0.1 mm and the shop profile does not list in-house CMM.

feasibility.assessment_notes: Proceed as a provisional near-net forged housing route using SPM/indexed fixturing. Published VMC travels are not adequate for full-envelope single-setup machining, but the profile includes SPM drilling/milling and tool-room fixture support; large-part fixture capacity must be confirmed before release.

starting_dimensions.notes: Near-net closed-die or open-die forged blank following the housing envelope, with approximately 3-5 mm machining allowance on datum/mating surfaces and additional allowance at ribs, bosses and heat-treat-critical faces. Envelope values shown are bounding-box planning values only, not a solid block recommendation.

stock.why: The part is a large 109 kg complex high-strength steel housing with ribs, bosses, curved saddle, multiple pockets and precision bores. Machining from a rectangular block near 681 x 319 x 454 mm would have very poor material utilization. For quantity 150 and 15CDV6 mechanical-property requirements, a near-net forging is preferred over casting; casting sequence was reviewed because the geometry resembles a housing/casting, but 15CDV6 and final heat-treatment requirements make forged stock the safer assumption.

evidence.cited_text: Envelope 671.1 x 309.0 x 443.9 mm; complex_3d housing with ribs, bosses and cavities

Datums are established first, all rough milling/hole generation occurs before heat treatment, burrs are removed before hardening, precision bores are finished after heat treatment, and cadmium plating is performed only after all machining and inspection preparation are complete.

clarifications.question: Confirm whether the starting blank is specified as forging, casting, or billet-machined stock.
clarifications.why_it_matters: The proposed route assumes near-net forging due to 15CDV6, 109 kg finished weight, complex geometry and quantity 150; a customer-mandated casting or billet would change stock, allowances and outside process sequence.
clarifications.suggested_default: Use near-net forged 15CDV6 blank unless the released drawing or customer specification states casting.

clarifications.question: Confirm that Almity's SPM milling/drilling equipment or partner capacity can hold and machine a 671.1 x 443.9 x 309 mm, 109 kg housing.
clarifications.why_it_matters: The listed vmc_3axis travels are smaller than the housing envelope; fixture/machine capacity is a route risk.
clarifications.suggested_default: Use SPM/indexed fixture or qualified large-machine supplier.

clarifications.question: Confirm all missing H7/H8 bore and hole depths/lengths, including F013, F046, F054, F055, F067 and F068.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Post-HT grinding/honing cycle inputs and tooling depend on bore/hole lengths.

clarifications.question: Confirm whether cadmium plating can be performed on the in-house plating_line or must be subcontracted.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Shop profile explicitly lists alkaline zinc plating, while the drawing requires cadmium 8-12 microns; approvals, chemistry, bake and environmental controls differ.
clarifications.suggested_default: Route to approved cadmium vendor if in-house line is zinc-only.

clarifications.question: Confirm exact pitch circle diameters for M8x1 bolt-circle patterns F017, F018 and F019.

clarifications.suggested_default: Do not use approximate Ø78 mm for released manufacturing without drawing confirmation.

clarifications.question: Confirm whether precision holes and threads are to be masked during cadmium plating or dimensioned to include 8-12 micron coating buildup.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Cadmium buildup can alter H7 fits and thread gauge results.
clarifications.suggested_default: Mask all H7/H8 holes, precision bores and threads unless the coating specification says otherwise.

clarifications.question: Confirm exact datum A, K and D_S2 surfaces and the final datum hierarchy for CMM inspection.

assumptions.text: Production quantity is 150 pieces, overriding the title-block quantity 1 for process selection.
Near-net forging is selected as starting stock because 15CDV6 is a forgeable alloy steel and machining the 109 kg complex housing from block would be highly wasteful.
SPM milling/drilling with dedicated fixtures can accommodate the large housing by indexing or extended supports, despite smaller published VMC travel.
Where hole or pocket depths are missing, formula_inputs leave depths null and use available diameter/count/area values only.
Heat treatment to 31-38 HRC is performed after rough/semi machining and before post-HT hard finishing of precision bores/datums.
Cadmium plating is performed after all machining; precision holes, bores and threads are masked unless customer specification confirms coating allowance.

analysis_trace.summary: The feature graph describes a very large complex 15CDV6 steel housing, approximately 671.1 x 443.9 x 309 mm and 109 kg, with broad datum faces, curved saddle, ribs, pockets, multiple M5/M8 threaded holes, Ø15 H7 and Ø11 H7 position-controlled holes, Ø38.5/Ø35.5 H8 coaxial bores, heat treatment to 31-38 HRC and cadmium plating 8-12 microns.
issues: Several hole depths, bore lengths, pocket depths and datum surfaces are missing or partly legible.
